name: Jacobi stationary linear solver
definition: Split A=D+L+U into diagonal, strict lower, and strict upper parts. Iterate x_(k+1)=D⁻¹[b−(L+U)x_k]. Convergence for every initial vector holds when ρ(−D⁻¹(L+U))<1.
variables: A coefficient matrix, b right-hand side, x iterate, ρ spectral radius
assumptions: Nonzero diagonal and contraction of the iteration matrix in spectral radius
limitations: Convergence can be slow for weak diagonal dominance and can fail even for some positive definite systems
failure_conditions: Convergence can be slow for weak diagonal dominance and can fail even for some positive definite systems
computation: O(nnz(A)) per sweep with parallel component updates

source.citation: Barrett et al., Templates for the Solution of Linear Systems, Netlib. https://www.netlib.org/templates/templates.html

name: Gauss–Seidel stationary linear solver
definition: With A=D+L+U, solve (D+L)x_(k+1)=b−Ux_k in increasing component order. Equivalently each update uses the latest already-computed lower-index entries.
variables: A coefficient matrix, D diagonal, L/U strict triangular parts, b right-hand side
assumptions: Nonzero diagonal; symmetric positive definite or strictly diagonally dominant A suffices for convergence
limitations: Ordering changes convergence and the triangular dependency limits naive parallelism
failure_conditions: Ordering changes convergence and the triangular dependency limits naive parallelism

source.citation: Barrett et al., Templates for the Solution of Linear Systems, Netlib. https://www.netlib.org/templates/templates.html

name: GMRES minimum-residual solver
definition: Set r₀=b−Ax₀ and K_k=span(r₀,Ar₀,…,A^(k−1)r₀). Compute x_k=argmin_(x∈x₀+K_k)‖b−Ax‖₂ using an Arnoldi orthonormal basis and its Hessenberg least-squares problem.
variables: A real square matrix, x₀ initial estimate, b right-hand side, k Krylov dimension
assumptions: Nonsingular A for the general full-dimensional exact-arithmetic claim; stop immediately if r₀=0
limitations: Basis growth increases memory, and restarting can stall
failure_conditions: Basis growth increases memory, and restarting can stall
computation: One matrix–vector product and O(kd) orthogonalization at step k for d unknowns

source.citation: Barrett et al., Templates for the Solution of Linear Systems, Netlib. https://www.netlib.org/templates/templates.html

application: Fit a coupled sparse linear state system whose coefficient matrix is nonsymmetric
required_inputs: A sparse square coefficient matrix, right-hand side and declared convergence tolerance from a historical fit or synthetic system.
data_rights: Use synthetic inputs or source-authorized historical records. Verify licence before acquisition.
incompatible_methods: Inputs first available after the forecast cutoff
mechanism_note: Residual minimization over a Krylov space. MINRES exploits symmetry via Lanczos and short recurrences.

name: MINRES symmetric minimum-residual solver
definition: For r₀=b−Ax₀ and β=‖r₀‖₂, build Lanczos basis V_k and tridiagonal extension T̄_k from A V_k=V_(k+1)T̄_k. Set x_k=x₀+V_k z where z minimizes ‖βe₁−T̄_k z‖₂, using sequential rotations and short recurrences.
variables: A symmetric system, β initial residual norm, e₁ first coordinate, V_k orthonormal, z reduced coefficients
assumptions: A real symmetric, possibly indefinite; stop immediately at β=0 and handle terminated Lanczos runs in their attained subspaces
limitations: Symmetry loss invalidates the short recurrence, and residual minimization alone does not guarantee a minimum-norm solution for singular problems
failure_conditions: Symmetry loss invalidates the short recurrence, and residual minimization alone does not guarantee a minimum-norm solution for singular problems
computation: One matrix–vector product and linear vector work per iteration with short updates

source.citation: SciPy maintainers’ minres reference and Barrett et al., Templates, Symmetric Lanczos Methods. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.sparse.linalg.minres.html
